answers.answer_text: The project uses the MIT License.

The two pass/fail npm checks are `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`. The full AGENTS.md pre-commit sequence runs `npm ci` first and also runs `npm run examples && git diff --exit-code examples/` to verify generated fixtures have not drifted.

Lexical P@1 improved by +33 to +83 percentage points on held-out questions across the three real repositories. No: the README says this shows that the metric is sensitive to real navigation edits, not that agent grounding improved; real-agent behavior is evaluated separately.

No. The repository is currently CLI-only and does not ship an MCP server. The roadmap places it in Phase 5, gated on Phase 4 establishing whether a better score changes agent grounding or exploration cost and therefore what product claim is supportable.
CI regenerates `examples/` and fails if the committed tree has moved. The one-word term is `drift`.

Semantic scoring requires `@huggingface/transformers` (version 4.2.0 in this repository). It is optional because its transitive onnxruntime-node/adm-zip and sharp/libvips dependency trees carry published security advisories, and a published package's overrides would not propagate to consumers; requiring an explicit install keeps the base installation dependency-light and clean while letting consumers control patched overrides.

The benchmarks are ContextBench and Agent Retrieval Bench. They hold the repository fixed and vary the retriever or agent, whereas this project holds the retriever fixed and varies the repository's navigation surface.
